overview: This file traces the U.S. occupation administration’s handling of a fourth-quarter 1946 allocation of abaca fiber for Japanese cordage manufacture. It begins with the Department of State’s tentative authorization of 685,000 pounds of spinnable fiber, plus monthly quantities of tow, continues with SCAP’s brief notice that action was pending, and concludes with a detailed request that the Reconstruction Finance Corporation confirm available grades and arrange shipment from the Philippines to Japan. The correspondence also records interagency clearances, the proposed landed-price calculation, and authorization to pay from the SCAP export fund.

subfiles.title: State Department authorization for Japanese abaca allocation
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department tentatively authorizes an abaca allocation for Japanese cordage production and instructs SCAP to begin negotiations with the Reconstruction Finance Corporation.
subfiles.summary: Pending formal Civilian Production Administration authorization, the Department tentatively establishes a fourth-quarter allocation of 685,000 pounds of spinnable abaca fiber in cordage grades J and below. It also reports that 100 tons of tow grades are available monthly and directs SCAP to begin negotiations with the Reconstruction Finance Corporation. Maguey and Canton fiber are stated not to fall under U.S. allocations, and the telegram records clearances from several U.S. agencies and offices.

subfiles.title: SCAP notice that action on the abaca allocation is pending
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State, Washington, via the War Department
subfiles.about: SCAP acknowledges the State Department’s abaca instruction and reports that a substantive reply will follow when action has been taken.
subfiles.summary: This short restricted relay refers to State Department telegram 481 of September 14. SCAP reports that action remains pending and promises a reply at the earliest opportunity. The page also documents the cable’s routing through the War Department and its receipt and filing by State Department offices.

subfiles.title: SCAP request for RFC confirmation and shipment of abaca
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: SCAP asks the Reconstruction Finance Corporation to confirm abaca quantities and grades, arrange shipment from the Philippines, and accept payment from the SCAP export fund.
subfiles.summary: SCAP requests confirmation and a shipping schedule for 685,000 pounds of spinnable abaca fiber in grades J and below for delivery during the fourth quarter of 1946, expressing a preference for higher grades. It separately seeks monthly quantities of 100 tons of abaca tow, again preferring higher grades. Prices are to equal the cost of comparable grades shipped to the United States plus freight and insurance to produce an FOB Japanese-port price. Payment to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation from the SCAP export fund is explicitly authorized.

interest: The file offers a compact view of how occupation authorities secured raw materials for Japan’s postwar industrial recovery through U.S.-controlled allocation and purchasing systems. Its unusually specific quantities, fiber grades, delivery period, pricing formula, and funding authorization make it useful for reconstructing the mechanics of commodity procurement rather than merely its policy aims. The routing marks and interagency clearances also reveal how the State Department, War Department, Civilian Production Administration, Reconstruction Finance Corporation, and SCAP divided responsibility and communicated across the occupation bureaucracy.
